# Sequence configuration, resources, and state

This guide separates three things that are easy to mix up: files packaged with a
Sequence, resources named by configuration, and state produced while an Instance
runs.

## Package files and external resources

**Packaged resources** are inside the uploaded Sequence archive: code,
dependencies, templates, and small static inputs. They are available from the
Sequence's package directory after deployment. A package is self-contained; the
Hub does not install missing Node dependencies for it.

**Configured external resources** are values such as a URL, object key, mounted
path, or credential reference supplied through Instance configuration. A
configuration value is only a description or pointer. It does not download,
mount, provision, or persist the resource by itself. The Sequence must be able
to reach the resource and should validate it before processing.

Keep secrets out of package files and logs. Treat configuration as untrusted
input and allow-list paths, hosts, and resource names before opening them.

## What the adapter can see

The adapter determines the process boundary, not the meaning of a configured
resource:

| Adapter | Files visible to the Sequence |
| --- | --- |
| Process | The host filesystem visible to the child process, subject to OS permissions and the configured working path. |
| Docker | The image/package plus paths and networks explicitly made available to the container. The host filesystem is not implicitly visible. |
| Kubernetes | The image/package plus paths, volumes, networks, and identity granted to the Pod. A Hub-side path is not implicitly a Pod path. |

Write examples against an explicit package-relative path or configured mount;
do not assume that a path on the Hub host exists in every Runner. A resource can
be packaged and readable while a configured external resource is absent or
inaccessible in the selected adapter.

## Summarize data at the source side

When the useful result is a compact description of a large local dataset, run
the Sequence where the source is accessible, validate and open the source once,
then stream summaries incrementally. There is no separate producer and no input
model containing precomputed results. A summary might contain relative file
names, row counts, byte counts, or schema information; it should not imply that
the Hub has copied or indexed the source dataset.

This pattern keeps source access and credentials at the source boundary. The
Sequence still needs access to the source, and any later read of the original
data remains subject to the selected adapter's visibility and permissions.

## State is application-owned

Transform Hub manages Instance lifecycle and transient stream delivery. It does
not provide runtime-managed checkpoints, replay, or durable application state.
If progress must survive a restart, choose and operate an external durable store
with the required consistency and recovery guarantees. `this.save()` is not a
documented persistence mechanism and must not be presented as one.

For installed execution of the source-summary pattern, use the [source-side data summary Process Adapter workflow](../examples/source-side-data-summary.md#installed-process-adapter-workflow), then refer to the [canonical installed Process Adapter example baseline](setup-and-run.md#installed-process-adapter-example-baseline). Maintainers may use `@scramjet/sequence-test` for optional local loading and execution evidence; it does not provide persistence or adapter-independent storage. Operate any durable store separately and test its consistency and recovery contract directly.
